definitions: To be essentially a matter of; to be the most important factor or aspect.
To be transmitted from an earlier time or generation.
To fall or descend, often referring to rain or snow.
To make a decision or judgment, often after consideration.
To criticize or reprimand someone severely.
examples: It all comes down to a lack of communication.
This tradition comes down from ancient times.
The rain comes down heavily every afternoon.
The ruling comes down on the side of the plaintiff.
The boss really comes down on anyone who is late.
